Fixture: 73_progressive_all_gray_128x128_nofilters.jxl
128x128 greyscale, VarDCT lossy, kLFFrame plus 2 shifted HF passes, d=1.0

Purpose
-------
Wave 5 (progressive decoding) acceptance fixture. The combination of 71 and 72, and the smallest stream with the same
feature set as the conformance case `progressive`: an LF frame
feeding a kUseLfFrame regular frame that is itself split into two
passes with a nonzero shift. Single group, so a failure here is not
about group geometry.

Frame structure, as parsed by JPXL itself (jpxl-decode's own frame-header
reader, not by any oracle):

  frame 0  kLFFrame       kModular  flags 0x0   lf_level 1
           num_passes 2, shift [1], 5 TOC sections
  frame 1  kRegularFrame  kVarDCT   flags 0x20 (kUseLfFrame)
           num_passes 2, shift [1], downsample [2], last_pass [0]
           1 group, 1 LF group, 5 TOC sections

The source content is the same shape as fixtures 50-57 use: the left half is
a smooth low-frequency ramp and the right half a 1-pixel checkerboard, the
highest spatial frequency a discrete grid can represent, so cjxl's own
transform-selection heuristic reaches for a mixture of varblock sizes. This
sidecar does not claim particular transforms were chosen.

--gaborish=0 --epf=0 disables both restoration filters. Per 18181-3 Annex A
Table A.1 that puts the stream in the tighter error class:

    Part 3 error class:  peak <= 0.004,  RMSE <= 1e-5   (no filters)

Grading is against a reference DECODE of this stream (the committed .npy, or a fresh djxl decode), never
against the original source PNM -- Part 3 conformance bounds
decoder-vs-reference error, not encoder loss against the pre-encode image.

    Committed alongside the fixture (< 100 KB).
    Shape (1, 128, 128, 1) little-endian f32, per 18181-3 4.1.2 -- djxl keeps a
    single-channel greyscale image as num_channels=1 rather than replicating
    it to RGB. Readable with jpxl_conformance::FloatImage::from_npy.
    Regenerable at any time from the fixture with the pinned djxl build
    (decode is deterministic per libjxl revision, see PINNED_REVISIONS.txt).

cjxl/djxl are used strictly as BLACK BOXES: they emit/consume conformant
streams for JPXL to parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a
different libjxl revision changes these digests, that is the point of
recording them -- do not silently update them; note the revision change.
